raw_response:
I'm 42 years old, a woman farmer in Quzhou County. I never went to school — not even one day — but I've been farming since I was a little girl helping my parents. Now I have 8 mu of land. My husband and my oldest son work construction in the city, so it's mostly me, my mother-in-law, and my younger daughter doing the farm work at home.

I grow wheat and maize on 5 mu — the double crop — and cotton on the other 3 mu. The wheat went in last October. I bought the seed from the shop in town, the common kind that everyone around here plants. For base fertilizer I put down about one big bag of that compound fertilizer per mu — the kind with the three numbers on the bag. Now it's spring and the wheat is greening up. I'll irrigate once soon, and when it gets to jointing I'll spread about half a bag of urea per mu. That's what I always do. If the leaves look yellow I might add a little more. I'll irrigate two more times before harvest — one at heading and one when the grain is filling. I spray for weeds once in spring, and if I see aphids I'll spray for those too. I expect about 400 kg per mu if the weather is normal, same as last year.

For cotton, I plant in mid-to-late April. I use the regular improved seed, not the fancy expensive hybrid kind. I put fertilizer in the furrow at planting — some compound fertilizer and a bit of phosphate. Then I topdress with urea when it starts flowering. Cotton needs water at the right time, so I irrigate twice — once when it flowers and once when the bolls are forming. I spray for insects three or four times, those bollworms are already bad this year. Picking is hard work. Me and my mother-in-law pick most of it, but I hire some women from the village to help during the busy weeks. I pay them by the jin picked. I hope for about 280 kg per mu of seed cotton if things go well.

The maize comes right after wheat. We harvest wheat in early June and have to plant maize fast — sometimes we only have a few days before the soil gets too dry. I buy hybrid maize seed, about 3 to 4 jin per mu. I plant and put compound fertilizer in the rows with the seed. If I have a little extra money after the wheat comes in, maybe I topdress with some urea when the maize is knee-high. Two irrigations for maize — one when it's small, one at tasseling. I spray herbicide after planting to keep the weeds down. I expect about 450 kg per mu.

Money is tight. I have about 4000 yuan for all the inputs and hired labor this season. The fertilizer is the most important — I won't skip that. I can't afford all the fancy stuff my neighbor Lao Wang buys for his bigger farm, but I do enough to get a decent crop. I don't take risks. If I'm not sure about something, I do what I did last year. A bad year hurts my family more than a good year helps us, so I'd rather put a little too much fertilizer than too little and lose the crop.
